blindSummary: Mixed picture: in 2024 this state/province recorded 16 killings of trans and gender-diverse people - the highest unit count that year - then fell to 4 recorded killings in 2025. The country's dominant geographic pattern applies here: at least 68% of the 2024 killings (83 of 122) happened outside capital cities, in interior cities, so the risk sits in this state/province's interior rather than its capital.
blindSourceSummaries: An encyclopaedia overview of the country's LGBT rights: relationship recognition (same-sex unions 2011, marriage 2013), the top court's 2018 self-declaration gender-identity rulings and treatment of non-binary markers, conversion-therapy and blood-donation positions, sections on anti-LGBT violence, religion and politics, and a summary table of legal status; used in the country-level assessment for the national legal baseline against which unit-level counts and ordinances diverge.

An international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations legal and legal gender recognition possible by self-determination, LGBT organisations able to register; marriage equality since 2013 with active legislative repeal efforts driven by anti-gender lawmakers; a 2019 top-court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds, yet the country keeps one of the highest recorded rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; over 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections.

A law-firm guide (updated April 2026) to LGBTQ+ legal rights for expats: no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute, but top-court rulings establish progressive protections - same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, adoption, and name/gender-marker changes; cited as the practical statement of the protective federal framework that state and municipal enforcement operates within.
blindLocalsOnly: The recorded killings are of local trans residents - the 2024 national victim profile is majority young, black and poor - rather than visitors; the protective federal machinery (name/gender change, hate-crime doctrine) is likewise resident-facing administrative law.
